problem_read.user_goal: Choose a PhD path while preserving fallback viability and avoiding false precision about outcomes.
knowns: The advisor may retire in 2-3 years.
The debated plan includes delayed reversal triggers.
Fallback viability depends on supervision and lab continuity.
unknowns: Whether the advisor will preserve the fallback path.
Whether funding remains available through the trigger date.
constraints: Do not use numeric success priors without grounding.
Do not assume the fallback remains open after delay.

deterministic_limit: Code validates custody, labels sources, and renders the deck; it does not decide cognitive usefulness.

step6_consideration_contract.decision_authority: Step 6 may use, reject, defer, or combine any card after serious consideration.
step6_consideration_contract.consideration_standard: For each card, form the strongest plausible application before setting it aside.
step6_consideration_contract.public_hygiene: Do not expose these private labels, source names, or card mechanics in the user-facing answer.
step6_consideration_contract.beyond_obvious_rule: Use the cards to go beyond the obvious when they reveal a non-obvious pressure, not to obey a template.
step6_consideration_contract.novelty_discipline: For each non-anchor card, decide whether it adds additive pressure, sharpens a condition, or is only confirming support. If it only confirms what the anchor already handles, keep it private unless restating it protects a concrete tripwire.

cards.cognitive_role: Concrete anchor: start from this because it preserves case-specific pressure in ordinary answer shape.
cards.anchor_text:
I would not choose the Silva direction yet, but I also would not default to the safer lab path. The decision should turn on two gates, not on which story feels more exciting or safer.

First, test whether Silva can become a dissertation: usable data you can access soon, a collaborator deep enough to offset your lab's lack of single-cell experience, and explicit advisor support. A hot field plus uncertain data is not a plan.

Second, protect the fallback while you test Silva. It is only real if it remains advisor-backed, resourced, technically ready, identity-coherent, and protected by a stop-loss date. Give the Silva probe a short, dated window and decide in advance what evidence makes you continue or stop.

The sequence is advisor first, low-cost Silva reality check second, committee only after you know whether the data path is real. Do not go around your advisor with a finished proposal, do not run all options in parallel, and do not treat broad PhD success-rate claims as probabilities for this case. With a three-month deadline and an advisor retiring in 2-3 years, choose only after both executability gates have evidence.
